# nish/sync/shm

Memory that several processes map at once, and the atomics that order what they write to it.

```ts
import {
  ACQUIRE,
  ACQ_REL,
  RELAXED,
  RELEASE,
  SEQ_CST,
  SHM_ACCESS,
  SHM_EXISTS,
  SHM_INVALID,
  SHM_NOT_EQUAL,
  SHM_NOT_FOUND,
  SHM_TIMED_OUT,
  SHM_TOO_MANY,
  SHM_UNSUPPORTED,
  SHM_WOKEN,
  SharedRegion,
  ShmError,
  createRegion,
  fence,
  openRegion,
  unlinkRegion,
} from "nish/sync/shm";
```

```ts
import { createRegion, openRegion, unlinkRegion, ACQUIRE, RELEASE } from "nish/sync/shm"

// The process that owns it: a fresh, zeroed region of 4096 bytes.
const stale = unlinkRegion("jobs") // a region a crashed run left, if any
const region = createRegion("jobs", 4096).expect("create")
region.storeI64(0, toI64(42), RELEASE)

// Any other process of the same user: the same bytes.
const view = openRegion("jobs").expect("open")
const n: i64 = view.loadI64(0, ACQUIRE) // 42 once the store is seen
```

<scalar-callout type="info">

**A region is a named POSIX shared-memory object** (`/dev/shm/<name>` on
Linux, `shm_open("/<name>")` on Darwin) mapped shared, so every process that
opens the name sees the same bytes. A name is 1 to 30 of `A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ -`,
not starting with `.`. `createRegion` makes it with mode 0600 and refuses a
name that exists (`SHM_EXISTS`), so a name another user planted is never
adopted; `openRegion` refuses a region this user does not own, that anyone
else may read or write, or (on Linux) that is not a regular file or has a
second hard link (`SHM_ACCESS`). The name stays until `unlinkRegion`,
even after every process has exited, which is how a process that starts later
finds it; the mapping goes away with `close` or with the process.

</scalar-callout>

<scalar-detail title="Why named, and no anonymous region made before fork">

A Nish program
has no `fork`: `spawn` and `nish/net/prefork` start a program with `exec`,
and every descriptor is close-on-exec, so neither an anonymous mapping nor a
`memfd` reaches the child. A name does. The supervisor creates the region
before `preforkWith`, every worker opens it by name, and the supervisor
unlinks it after (`examples/prefork-jobs.ts`, docs/wp47-shared-memory.md).

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="Every access is checked">

An offset is an `i32` byte offset into the
region. A 32-bit slot sits at a multiple of 4 and a 64-bit one at a multiple
of 8, wholly inside the region; a byte copy fits the region and the buffer.
Anything else panics, naming the offset and the region's size, exactly as an
array index out of range does. An ordering an access cannot take (a load
with `RELEASE`) panics too. A region is never read or written past its end.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="Orderings are C11's">

`RELAXED`, `ACQUIRE`, `RELEASE`, `ACQ_REL` and
`SEQ_CST`; a load takes the first, second and last, a store the first, third
and last, and a read-modify-write any of them. Each access is one LLVM
atomic instruction on the speed and size profiles, where the runtime is
inlined into the program; a compare-exchange that fails orders as C++
derives it (`ACQ_REL` fails `ACQUIRE`, `RELEASE` fails `RELAXED`). Bytes
copied by `read` and `write` are plain copies, ordered by the atomics around
them, and a copy that races a writer in another process can be torn but is
never read past its window.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="Waiting">

`waitI32` sleeps while a 32-bit slot holds a value and `wake`
wakes the processes sleeping on it: Linux's futex, shared between processes.
Darwin and wasi answer `SHM_UNSUPPORTED` (-95) from both, as
`setIdlePriority` does on Darwin, and a program there polls instead.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="A region belongs to the thread that mapped it">

Under `--threads` the
runtime's table of regions is thread-local, so a `SharedRegion` handed to
another thread names nothing there and panics; that thread opens the name
again. Native only: `--emit-ts` refuses a module that declares C functions,
and creating a region on wasi answers `SHM_UNSUPPORTED`. Calling C is the
`ffi` capability, so a program that imports this module is reported with
`ffi` and `--deny ffi` refuses it.

</scalar-detail>

Private helpers share the importing program's flat symbol namespace
(`docs/wp26-stdlib.md` §3e), which is why each one carries the module's name.

## createRegion

Creates the region `name`, `bytes` long and zeroed, mode 0600, and maps it.
`SHM_EXISTS` when the name is taken: unlink a stale one first.

```ts
function createRegion(
  name: string,
  bytes: i32,
): Result<SharedRegion, ShmError>
```

## openRegion

Maps the region `name` that some process of this user created. Its size is
the region's (on Darwin, rounded up to a page).

```ts
function openRegion(
  name: string,
): Result<SharedRegion, ShmError>
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="name" type="string" required>
</scalar-field>

#### Returns

<scalar-field name="returns" type="Result&lt;SharedRegion, ShmError&gt;">
</scalar-field>

## unlinkRegion

Removes the name, so no process can open it again; every mapping of it
stays valid until it is closed. `SHM_NOT_FOUND` when there is none.

```ts
function unlinkRegion(
  name: string,
): Result<void, ShmError>
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="name" type="string" required>
</scalar-field>

#### Returns

<scalar-field name="returns" type="Result&lt;void, ShmError&gt;">
</scalar-field>

## SharedRegion

A mapped region. Every slot offset is in bytes from its start; an offset
outside it, a misaligned slot or an ordering the access cannot take panics.

```ts
class SharedRegion
```

| Member | |
| --- | --- |
| `new SharedRegion(handle: i32)` |  |
| `handle: i32` | The runtime's handle; it names nothing after `close`. |
| `addI32(at: i32, delta: i32, order: i32): i32` | Adds `delta` to the 32-bit slot at `at`, wrapping, and answers the value before. |
| `addI64(at: i32, delta: i64, order: i32): i64` | Adds `delta` to the 64-bit slot at `at`, wrapping, and answers the value before. |
| `close(): Result<void, ShmError>` | Unmaps the region; the handle names nothing after. The name stays until `unlinkRegion`. |
| `compareExchangeI32(at: i32, expected: i32, desired: i32, order: i32): i32` | Sets the 32-bit slot at `at` to `desired` if it holds `expected`, and answers what it held: the exchange happened when that is `expected`. |
| `compareExchangeI64(at: i32, expected: i64, desired: i64, order: i32): i64` | Sets the 64-bit slot at `at` to `desired` if it holds `expected`, and answers what it held: the exchange happened when that is `expected`. |
| `exchangeI32(at: i32, value: i32, order: i32): i32` | Sets the 32-bit slot at `at` to `value` and answers the value before. |
| `exchangeI64(at: i32, value: i64, order: i32): i64` | Sets the 64-bit slot at `at` to `value` and answers the value before. |
| `giveBack(window: u8[]): i32` | Empties `window`, which this region lent, and answers the length it had. |
| `lend(at: i32, len: i32, reuse: u8[] \| null = null): u8[]` | A `u8[]` of length `len` whose bytes are the region's `[at, at + len)`, not a copy: an index or `copyBytes` into it reads and writes the region. A range outside the region panics. `giveBack` or `close` empties it (length 0), so an index after either panics. A `push` moves it into this process's own memory, after which it is no window and `giveBack` panics. Pass a window already given back as `reuse` to lend it again without a new header: each lend without one keeps a few bytes for the life of the process. |
| `loadI32(at: i32, order: i32): i32` | The 32-bit slot at `at`. |
| `loadI64(at: i32, order: i32): i64` | The 64-bit slot at `at`. |
| `read(at: i32, dst: u8[], off: i32, len: i32): void` | Copies `len` bytes of the region at `at` into `dst[off, off + len)`. |
| `size(): i32` | The region's length in bytes. |
| `storeI32(at: i32, value: i32, order: i32): void` | Sets the 32-bit slot at `at` to `value`. |
| `storeI64(at: i32, value: i64, order: i32): void` | Sets the 64-bit slot at `at` to `value`. |
| `waitI32(at: i32, expected: i32, timeoutMs: i32): i32` | Sleeps while the 32-bit slot at `at` holds `expected`, at most `timeoutMs` (negative: no limit): `SHM_WOKEN`, `SHM_NOT_EQUAL`, `SHM_TIMED_OUT`, or `SHM_UNSUPPORTED` off Linux. |
| `wake(at: i32, count: i32): i32` | Wakes at most `count` of the processes sleeping on the 32-bit slot at `at`: how many it woke, or `SHM_UNSUPPORTED` off Linux. |
| `write(at: i32, src: readonly u8[], off: i32, len: i32): void` | Copies `src[off, off + len)` into the region at `at`. |

## ShmError

Why a region could not be created, opened, unlinked or closed.

```ts
class ShmError
```

| Member | |
| --- | --- |
| `new ShmError(code: i32)` |  |
| `code: i32` | The errno, positive: `SHM_NOT_FOUND`, `SHM_EXISTS` and the rest. |
| `message: string` | What it means, such as `File exists`. |

<scalar-card title="2" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

A load that sees everything written before the `RELEASE` store it reads.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="4" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`ACQ_REL: i32`

A read-modify-write that is both.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="0" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`RELAXED: i32`

No ordering beyond the access itself being whole.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="3" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`RELEASE: i32`

A store after which everything written before it is seen by an `ACQUIRE` load of it.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="5" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`SEQ_CST: i32`

One order every `SEQ_CST` access in every process agrees on.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="13" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`SHM_ACCESS: i32`

`ShmError.code`: another user's region, one others may use, or not one region under one name.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="17" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`SHM_EXISTS: i32`

`ShmError.code`: a region of that name exists already.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="22" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`SHM_INVALID: i32`

`ShmError.code`: a name that is not 1 to 30 of `A-Za-z0-9._-`, or a size outside 1 byte to 1 GiB.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="-11" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`SHM_NOT_EQUAL: i32`

`waitI32`: the slot did not hold the value, so it did not sleep.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="2" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`SHM_NOT_FOUND: i32`

`ShmError.code`: no region of that name.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="-110" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`SHM_TIMED_OUT: i32`

`waitI32`: the time ran out.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="24" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`SHM_TOO_MANY: i32`

`ShmError.code`: this thread has 63 regions open.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="-95" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`SHM_UNSUPPORTED: i32`

`waitI32` and `wake` on Darwin and wasi, and every region on wasi: not here.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="0" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`SHM_WOKEN: i32`

`waitI32`: woken, or for no reason the caller can see; load the slot again.
